rated_messages.input_message: Some people find it helpful to give a name to their urge. If you're experiencing regular urges, give that feeling a name ('Olga the urge'?), and tell it that you won't give in to it. It may make it easier to live with (e.g. "ok Olga, I need to be by myself now...").
No need to get rid of these feelings or control them with a smoke. They are not permanent.
Setting small goals when you feel unmotivated is best. Maybe a small goal for now is to breathe deeply for the next 3 minutes instead of smoking.
What inspires you most to quit smoking? Are you willing to let this urge pass without smoking for that reason?
Practice staying in this location without smoking. Just notice your urge. Practicing this will weaken this trigger with time. Just think of it as practice.
Take a deep breath. Focus on today and the things you have accomplished. How many urges have you let pass? Give yourself some credit!
Imagine your 'you' from next year has come to visit, and guess what? You quit! How good is that?
To help get through a 'risky situation', remind yourself of how far you've come and the effort that you've put in. Don't ruin your hard work - stay strong!
If this situation becomes stressful for you, make an excuse to leave for a few minutes. If this doesn't help, it might be better to just leave early.
Pause and take 5 slow breaths. Pausing just for a moment breaks the automatic habit of reaching for a smoke.
